Every input goes to one folder, the store, which all services share, so a layer that two services use is downloaded once.
`esa inputs` lists the inputs with their state, and `esa fetch` downloads what is missing. The fetchers write each file under a
temporary name and rename it when it is complete, so an interrupted download leaves nothing half written. The code annex of each
service page describes what its fetchers do, and the [catalogue](https://github.com/renatovargas/esa-toolbox/blob/main/src/esa_toolbox/data/catalog.py)
and the [fetchers](https://github.com/renatovargas/esa-toolbox/blob/main/src/esa_toolbox/data/fetch.py) hold the code.

| `gdmp_annual` | Gross Dry Matter Productivity, version 2, annual sum of 36 ten-day values, 1 km (2000 to 2018) and 300 m (2018, 2024) | @copernicus2020gdmp1km; @copernicus2020gdmp300 | wood, carbon | 1.1 |
| `roads` | Motorways, trunk and primary roads with their links, rasterised at 100 m | @osm2026, through @klab2026 | pollination | 0.8 |

## Releases

Corine, the NUTS boundaries, the productivity, the bumblebee model, the crop data and version 32.0e of E-OBS are fixed releases,
so a new download gives the same files. The E-OBS layers need a download of 2.1 GB, which the fetcher removes once it has written
the five small files that the tool keeps. The fitted bumblebee models and the elevation layer that they read travel inside the
package, as the page on crop pollination explains. Eurostat revises its datasets with each release, and so the fetcher records the date of retrieval of every extract in
the file `extracts.json` beside it. The report of each run lists its inputs with those dates. Eurostat publishes the EU27 price index
from 2000, and the fetcher estimates the years before from the rates of the euro area and the other Member States, as the page on crop
pollination explains.

## Keys

The annual productivity needs a free account of the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem with S3 keys, in the variables
`CDSE_S3_ACCESS_KEY` and `CDSE_S3_SECRET_KEY`. The tool never writes the keys to a file or a log. Reading the 180 files of the
productivity takes several hours, and all other inputs take a few minutes.
